strategy.summary: Reproduce scikit-learn convergence bug in `SGDOneClassSVM` where, with `tol != None`, convergence/stopping uses only loss/error instead of the full objective (including regularization), causing premature stopping (typically too small `n_iter_`). The reproducing test is `test_sgd_oneclass_convergence`, which asserts `model.n_iter_ > 6` for several `nu` values.

strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision (`86906384af8f`), the test fails because `model.n_iter_` becomes `<= 6` (premature stopping) for at least one of `nu in [0.1, 0.5, 0.9]`, violating `assert model.n_iter_ > 6`. On the fixed revision (the PR's post-fix commit), the same test passes because convergence uses the full objective (with regularization) when `tol!=None`, so `model.n_iter_ > 6` for all three `nu` values.
strategy.numerical_probe: Assert-based probe: `model.n_iter_` after `SGDOneClassSVM(..., max_iter=100, tol=1e-3, learning_rate='constant', eta0=1e-3).fit(iris.data)`; bug shows premature stopping around ~6 epochs/iterations, i.e., `n_iter_` does not exceed 6.

risks: The defect is primarily triggered when `tol != None` (default early stopping criteria); using `tol=None` may not reproduce the premature-stopping behavior.

The observed premature stopping is described as “almost always after ~6 epochs” but exact `n_iter_` can vary by BLAS/threads and numerical details; however, the test only checks `n_iter_ > 6`, so environment drift must not push fixed behavior down to `<= 6`.

Build/toolchain differences (compiler, OpenBLAS implementation, architecture) may change convergence timing; if the bug is sensitive to floating-point/threads, the failure might not transition reliably on non-matching platforms.
